IncidentBot: paging Maya (oncall) — streaming service p99 latency spike detected on EU-proxy cluster, metric streaming.sse.proxy_write_latency.p99 = 12.3s (> SLO 5s). alert_id=INC-6798
Maya (oncall): ack. looking.
Maya (oncall): quick check — is this limited to EU region? @Raj can you confirm cross-region? link: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/streaming
Raj (eng-sre): seen same in us-west but smaller (p99 ~3.8s). EU is blown out. dashboard shows sudden tail increase starting 6798884200.
Tori (eng-runtime): any recent runtime deploys to streaming-proxy? @deploy-bot rollouts?
deploy-bot: deploys: streaming-proxy service had a canary 6798879000 -> stable 6798879800, patch "chunk-coalesce fix" rolled at 6798879800.
Maya (oncall): OK, correlate traces. running sample query for slow traces.
Maya (oncall): trace ids: 9f3a2b, a7c11d showing long write waits at proxy flush() and connection buffer backpressure.
Leo (eng-infra): nginx upstream_write_timeouts spiked in EU-proxy logs. also see many connections with client_rbuffer_full. suspect client backpressure + bigger server-side chunks.
ops_cb (CS): CS: we have 7 enterprise customers reporting intermittent stalls, 2 on EU region. one reported full stall for ~20s. customer: AcmeAnalytics (prod).
Raj (eng-sre): quick mitigations: 1) reduce proxy chunk size threshold to force smaller chunks; 2) enable short-chunk-mode; 3) bump keepalive timeout? prefer non-invasive first.
Tori (eng-runtime): I can flip short-chunk-mode on EU-proxy nodes. command:
```
# enable short-chunk on EU proxies
curl -XPOST https://controlplane.redwood/api/proxy/config -d '{"cluster":"eu-proxy","short_chunk":true}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN'
```
Maya (oncall): please do it on canary subset (10%) first, watch p99.
Tori (eng-runtime): doing canary now -> /control confirm 10% applied to nodes eu-proxy-0-2
Tori (eng-runtime): applied. monitoring.
Raj (eng-sre): observing rolling drop in p99 for canary nodes: from 12.3s -> 3.6s within 30s.
Maya (oncall): nice. start ramp to 50% if no regressions.
Tori (eng-runtime): ramping. also opening temporary proxy-level buffer tuning to reduce NGINX proxy_buffer_size from 8k -> 4k to avoid big upstream writes.
Leo (eng-infra): note — lowering buffer increases syscalls but reduces single large write latency. CPU impact minimal on canary.
ops_cb (CS): CS: notify AcmeAnalytics support now with workaround and ETA. they want incident number.
Maya (oncall): sending short update to customers: "We're mitigating intermittent streaming stalls in EU — temporary proxy change applied; monitoring. If you see resumed streams, no action needed. Incident link: https://status.redwood.example/INC-6798 :thumbsup:"
ops_cb (CS): noted, sending.
Raj (eng-sre): after ramp to 50% p99 across cluster down to ~2.2s. EU overall p95 ~430ms now. continuing ramp.
Tori (eng-runtime): one regression observed on node eu-proxy-4 — increased tail CPU and GC pauses likely unrelated. rolling back short-chunk there and excluding it from ramp.
Maya (oncall): good catch. exclude problematic node and continue.
Maya (oncall): root-cause hypothesis: recent "chunk-coalesce" change (rolled earlier) increased average chunk sizes to reduce token overhead; combined with some clients that apply strong backpressure, large chunks cause upstream proxy write stalls when clients stop reading -> proxy buffers fill -> long write latencies -> p99 spike. temporary mitigation = force smaller chunks + proxy buffer tuning. long-term: fix runtime to be adaptive to client read-window and implement backpressure-aware chunking.
Raj (eng-sre): action items:
- short-term: keep short-chunk-mode for EU until full fix (owner: Tori) — ETA 6h
- investigate canary failure node eu-proxy-4 (owner: Leo) — ETA 2h
- create regression test for client backpressure (owner: Tori/Raj) — ETA 3d
- postmortem if impact to paying customers confirmed (owner: Maya) — ETA 48h
ops_cb (CS): CS tracking: impacted customers list + timeline. will coordinate with account owners.
Maya (oncall): summary to handoff -> Raj takes on-call for next shift at 6798884600. I'm leaving notes in the incident doc and adding playbook steps.
Raj (eng-sre): taking handoff. current state: mitigation (short-chunk-mode) rolled to 80% excluding eu-proxy-4; overall p99 EU=2.1s, p95=410ms. alerts suppressed for now (will re-enable if >5s).
Maya (oncall): thanks team. followups: schedule post-incident eval, capture traces & sample payloads, add e2e test for streaming stalls. I'm marking this as handoff -> Raj. :white_check_mark:
deploy-bot: noted — create deploy audit for 6798879800 canary -> stable.
IncidentBot: incident INC-6798 updated: mitigation applied, handoff to Raj. Notifications sent to affected customers.
Maya (oncall): leaving channel.
Raj (eng-sre): I'll coordinate next steps and post final timeline once we confirm all customers stable.
